data_products.ShortText: Provides key data about employee absence patterns and helps in absence metrics analysis.
data_products.Description:
This data product includes measures such as Total Absence Duration Days, both in full and in proportional value (pro rata), to provide insights into the total number of days that the employees are absent and the adjusted absence durations based on specific factors. The data product also tracks the Total Number of Absence Occurrences to measure frequency. These measures collectively enable comprehensive analysis of absence trends, frequency, and severity across the workforce.

**Business Context**: Delivers essential insights into employee absence patterns, supporting effective analysis of absence-related metrics.

data_products.ShortText: Provides event-based data with one record per requisition recorded against the fill date, and one record per requisition recorded against the hire date.
data_products.Description:
This data product tracks the number of calendar days from when a hiring requisition is raised until a successful applicant accepts the job offer and starts work, segmented by key dimensions such as status, recruiter, and location. A project is a structured endeavor with defined objectives, timelines, and budgets to achieve a unique outcome.  A project is characterized by a unique set of conditions on which it is based (for example, the targets to be met, the organizational structure, and the financial, personal, staffing and time constraints on the project).

data_products.Description:
A Cost Origin Group is an organizational unit, and a grouping mechanism, used to subdivide costs. It breaks down material and overhead costs into subdivisions within a general ledger account. When calculating material and overhead costs, they are assigned to a general ledger account. The combination of the origin group and general ledger account helps define calculation bases for determining overhead rates for specific material groups. It also defines cost components in product costing for particular material groups, and creates rules for activating work in process for each material group.
The following are possible values: 
01: Open
02: Released

Each cost center is assigned a category, depending on its type, such as Marketing (9), Production (F), Development (E), and other types.

data_products.Description:
A general ledger account represents G/L Account Master Data in the Chart of Accounts area which contain information about the G/L account that are valid for all company codes. The chart of accounts area also contains data that control how a G/L account is created in the company code-specific area.

Examples:
(1) Information if the G/L Account is a Profit & Loss Account
(2) Description of the G/L Account

**Business Context**: General Ledger Account is concerned with processing and reporting all postings relevant to external financial accounting. Due to the nature of the Universal Journal, the process also includes elements of internal accounting (Controlling).
As part of these activities, General Ledger Account line items are processed, which potentially contains personal data.
The DP is intended to be used for financial accounting, ensuring accurate, auditable, and compliant financial reporting.

data_products.Description:
A country is a coded representation of the country/region key that contains information which is also used to validate entries such as the length of the postal code or bank account number. Usually, the two-character ISO code in accordance with ISO 3166, which is delivered by SAP as a default is used. It could also be the vehicle license plate country/region code or a typical country/region key. For example, in Germany the Federal Statistical Office key. The definition of the country/region keys in the SAP system does not necessarily have to match political or state units. It must be noted that the the country/region key does not have to correspond to the ISO code in all installations.

_BusinessObjectsDetail.Name: sap-odm-CreditMemoRequest-v1
_BusinessObjectsDetail.Description: A credit memo request is a sales document used to propose a reduction in customer-specific receivables in the context of sales.

_FullDetail.ShortText: A credit memo request is a sales document used to propose a reduction in customer-specific receivables in the context of sales.
_FullDetail.Description:
A credit memo request is a sales document used to propose a reduction in customer-specific receivables in the context of sales. It is used to request a credit for a customer for reasons such as:

  • The customer returns goods previously purchased and needs to be credited for the returned items.
  • The customer asks for compensation for defective goods without returning them.
  • The customer has paid more than the invoiced amount and requests a credit to correct the excess amount.

Once approved, the system uses the credit memo request to create a credit memo.

_FullDetail.Description:
A debit memo request is a sales document used to propose an increase in customer-specific receivables. It's used to request additional charges on a customer for reasons such as:

_BusinessObjectsDetail.Name: sap-odm-PreliminaryBillingDocument-v1
_BusinessObjectsDetail.Description: A preliminary billing document is a set of data that serves as an optional, intermediary business document between a billed reference document (for example, a billing document request) and the final billing document (usually an invoice).

_FullDetail.ShortText: A preliminary billing document is a set of data that serves as an optional, intermediary business document between a billed reference document (for example, a billing document request) and the final billing document (usually an invoice).
_FullDetail.Description:
A preliminary billing document is a set of data that serves as an optional, intermediary business document between a billed reference document (for example, a billing document request) and the final billing document (usually an invoice).
 
Preliminary billing documents are almost identical to standard billing documents in form and content, but are created purely for negotiation purposes. Like billing documents, preliminary billing documents consist of a header and a number of items. The header contains data that applies to the entire document (for example, the billing date and the bill-to party), while the items contain data that is only valid for the respective item (for example, the sold product, its quantity, and its net value). 
 
Preliminary billing documents are relevant for output (for example, print), but not for posting to financial accounting.

_BusinessObjectsDetail.Name: sap-odm-BillingDocumentRequest-v1
_BusinessObjectsDetail.Description: A billing document request (BDR) is a set of data that acts as an intermediary business document between raw, itemized billable data and the subsequent billing documents.

_FullDetail.ShortText: A billing document request (BDR) is a set of data that acts as an intermediary business document between raw, itemized billable data and the subsequent billing documents.
_FullDetail.Description:
A billing document request (BDR) is a set of data that acts as an intermediary business document between raw, itemized billable data and the subsequent billing documents. 

In a BDR, the system persists this billable data in a header-and-item-based document format. The header contains data that applies to the entire document (for example, the billing date and the bill-to party). The items contain data that is only valid for the respective item (for example, the sold product, its quantity, and its net value). 

 

BDRs serve to funnel itemized billable data from a range of system-internal and external sources into the billing process. For example, billable data originating from service transactions, from an imported spreadsheet file, or from an integrated external system can all be persisted in the system as BDRs.

BDRs can be billed, individually or together with other sales and distributions (SD) documents, to create customer invoices and other billing documents. They appear in the billing due list alongside other billable SD documents.

data_products.Description:
A consolidation financial statement item is a fundamental account assignment in group reporting and financial consolidation. It forms the basis for data collection, posting, and reporting. It can also be used for maintaining metrics and key figures.

**Business Context**: The data product contains data intended to be used for financial consolidation. In addition, the data product contains personal data regarding business users that is intended to be used for administrative information.

data_products.Description:
A Consolidation Subitem determines the values for a given subitem category, such as transaction types or functional areas. The subitem category together with the subitem can determine a further breakdown of the financial statement items. This definition happens in the breakdown category. 

Example values of subitem category 1 are: 900 for Opening balance, 901 for Incoming units, 906 for Dividends, 909 for Change in accounting policies, 915 for Net variation, 920 for Increase/ Purchase, 950 for Reclassification, 955 for Fair value,980 for Currency translation adjustment.
Examples values of subitem category 2 are: YB10 for Sales Revenue, YB18 Cost of Goods Sold, YB20 for Production, YB40 for Administration.

_BusinessObjectsDetail.Name: sap-odm-ConsolidationSubitem-v1
_BusinessObjectsDetail.Description: A consolidation subitem is a value within a given subitem category in financial consolidation.

_FullDetail.ShortText: A consolidation subitem is a value within a given subitem category in financial consolidation.
_FullDetail.Description:
A consolidation subitem is a value within a given subitem category in financial consolidation. The subitem category together with the subitem may determine a further breakdown of a financial statement item. Whether such a further breakdown of a financial statement item by subitem category and subitem is mandatory, optionally allowed, or even not allowed is defined in the breakdown category which is assigned in the master data of the financial statement item.

Example values of subitem category 1 for transaction types are:

  • 900: Opening balance
  • 901: Incoming units

Example values of subitem category 2 for functional areas are:

  • YB10: Sales revenue
  • YB18: Cost of goods sold

- 12: Standardizing entry: Consolidation group change
- 20: Two-sided elimination: Entry
- 22: Two-sided elimination: Consolidation group change
- 30: Consolidation entry

data_products.Description:
A consolidation version is a distinct version of data in consolidation. In addition to a consolidation version for actual data, other versions of data that can be managed in parallel can be created, so that alternative results for the purposes of simulation, planning, and restatement can be produced. A consolidation version can be used for parallel processing with different data categories, accounting principles, and valuations, such as multiple group currencies.
To each consolidation version, special versions are assigned. The assignment of special versions enables the reuse of the maintained settings of a special version among different consolidation versions: The control parameters are entered only once in a special version and these settings are then reflected in all the consolidation versions to which the special version is assigned. Examples for special versions are data entry, consolidation unit attributes, financial statement item attributes, group structure, exchange rates, reclassification and elimination.

**Business Context**:

data_products.ShortText: Data Product Bill Of Material Configuration Data
data_products.Description: Bill of Material Configuration Data contains data as well as coded representations that are used for the configuration of bills of material (BOMs). The data contains information which is configured by the customer as well as SAP-defined code list values for bill of material processes. The following SAP object types and code lists are provided: Bill of Material Item Category with the following possible values: C: Compatible Unit D: Document item E: Enhanced Limit I: PM structure element K: Class item L: Stock item M: Intra material N: Non-stock item P: Preliminary Item R: Variable-size item S: Non-Plant Item T: Text item Bill of Material Status with the following possible values: 01: Active 02: Inactive 03: Active with history reqmt Bill of Material Variant Usage with the following possible values: 1: Production 2: Engineering/Design 3: Universal 4: Plant Maintenance 5: Sales and Distribution 6: Costing 7: Empties 8: Stability Study B: Sales Bundles (IS-HT-SW)C:Configuration Control J: JIT production line supply M: External Munitions Display P: Predictive MRP S: Service Management U: IUID Embedded Items Bill of Material Version Status with the following possible values: 01: In Process 99: Released 90: Obsolete
data_products.Industries: High Tech,Mill Products,Industrial Machinery and Components

_OutputPortsDetail.Description: Data Product Bill Of Material Configuration Data

Recruiting delivers the following primary data products: Interview Assessments: Includes feedback, ratings, comments, and other evaluation details. Interview Slots: Captures scheduled times, interviewer and candidate information, and status updates. We ingest both historical and ongoing interview assessment and slot data from Recruiting into our BDC. This process ensures a comprehensive and up-to-date view of interview activities and performance, supporting informed decision-making and continuous improvement across HR functions.

**Business Context**: By capturing interview assessments and scheduling details, this data enables HR to track progress and make well-informed decisions based on the latest updates.

data_products.Description:
A contract accounting document (FI-CA document) is a document in the Contract Accounting sub-ledger.
Contract accounting documents consist of header data, business partner items and general ledger items.
In addition to the unique document number, the header data also contains the document type as the classifying attribute, the currency key and various date specifications.
All items contain the posting amount and the necessary information for General Ledger Accounting, Cash Management and Controlling.
The items in contract accounts also contain specifications regarding the due date, cash discount, for controlling dunning, automatic payments or debit memos as well as for calculating interest.
data_products.Industries: Public Sector,High Tech,Mill Products,Industrial Machinery and Components

data_products.Description:
A contract accounting invoicing document is a commercial document issued to a customer, containing details of a receivable or credit. An invoicing document is used as a statement to justify a receivable for a provided service, notify the receiver about a certain credit, or inform the receiver about unpaid invoices, interests, or dunning fees. An invoicing document contains information about the amount due, payment terms, provided service, taxation, and in some countries special information assigned by public authorities, such as official document numbers.

**Business Context**: The data product contains potentially personal data that is intended to be used in invoice management in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable
data_products.Industries: Public Sector,High Tech,Mill Products,Industrial Machinery and Components

**Business Context**: Tracks employee participation in allowance benefits by capturing enrollment information, amounts, and effective dates throughout the benefit lifecycle.

A workforce pension enrollment data product is responsible for managing pension enrollments along with their associated contribution details. It is used to track an employee’s participation in the pension benefit, including enrollment information, contribution amounts, and effective dates.

**Business Context**: Tracks employee participation in pension benefits by managing enrollment information, contribution amounts, and effective dates throughout the pension lifecycle.

data_products.Description:
A workforce insurance benefit is a data product responsible for managing the configuration of insurance plans within an organization. It is used to define the insurance plans, tier options, and the coverages related to an insurance plan.

**Business Context**: Manages insurance benefit configurations, coverage options, and eligibility criteria to enable various insurance types such as health, life, dental, and disability coverage.

A workforce pension benefit is a data product responsible for managing the configuration of pension plans within an organization. It is used to define enrollment rules, eligibility criteria, and contribution structures. This includes setting up employee and employer contribution options such as employee with employer match as well as configuring minimum and maximum contribution limits for additional voluntary contributions.

**Business Context**: Defines pension plan configurations, enrollment rules, and contribution structures to establish employee and employer contribution options with appropriate voluntary contribution limits.

_OutputPortsDetail.Name: sap-bdc-sf-benefits-PensionBenefit-v1
_OutputPortsDetail.Description: A Pension Benefit data product has the information about the pension type benefit set up by benefit administrators.

data_products.ShortText: This data product provides information about the types of employee absence and its occurrences.
data_products.Description:
The Absence Data Product provides information about an employee’s absences. This includes the absence request itself, which is a record of an absence occurrence for an employee. It has attributes such as start date and end date, start time and end time, approval status, and various quantities like quantity in days, hours, or weeks. The data product also includes the absence type, which is a logical grouping of absence requests. It is used to specify the group characteristics, for example, whether an absence request represents a vacation or sick leave. It also restricts the allowed values for attributes of the absence request.

**Business Context**: This data product delivers insights into the various types of employee absences and their frequency of occurrence.

_OutputPortsDetail.Name: sap-bdc-sf-timemanagement-Absence-v1
_OutputPortsDetail.Description: This data product provides information about the types of employee absence and its occurrences.

data_products.ShortText: This data product provides information regarding the times and dates on which an employee is scheduled to work.
data_products.Description:
This data product provides information on the scheduled working hours for an individual employee on a specific calendar day. It is derived from the work schedule, public holidays, and substitutions (temporary changes). In addition to the date for which the planned working time applies, it also includes attributes like the start time and end time, the working time duration, and an indication of whether a particular day is a holiday or not. To enable comparisons between the original planned values based on the employee’s master data and the actual planned values, which can be influenced by public holidays and temporary changes, the start time and end time, as well as the duration based on both the original values and the actual values, are included in the data product.

**Business Context**:

_OutputPortsDetail.Name: sap-bdc-sf-timemanagement-WorkforcePlannedWorkingTime-v1

data_products.Description:
A condition contract is a document to manage conditions negotiated with a business partner. It represents an agreement on the conditions which can either accompany an invoice such as prices or discounts, or may require a subsequent settlement. The object covers a variety of information, such as the agreed settlement terms and conditions, the pricing records, as well as the agreed scope of the subsequent settlement.

**Business Context**: The data product contains potentially personal data that represents master data for managing condition contracts and is intended to be used in different business processes related to that data.

A treasury ledger position is an entity that carries the values of your financial instruments according to accounting principles. It is used to break down the balance sheet accounts in the treasury subledger. For a financial instrument, there is a treasury ledger position in each valuation area. An accounts receivable bank statement is a periodically issued record of the balance in a bank account and displays the sum of deposits and withdrawals. As it is relevant to financial operations, such as receivables management and invoice management, the bank statement is used to report and verify all recorded transactions as part of financial reconciliation processes.

**Business Context**: The data product potentially contains personal data that is intended to be used for the financial reconciliation processing.

data_products.Description: The Cash Flow is a key measurement of health for a company's financial status, includes cash receipts and cash payments over a given period of time. Cash flows can be actual cash flows which are confirmed by banks, and forecasted cash flows which are planned but not confirmed yet. Cash flows can be from different business components, for instance, sales, purchase, account payable, account receivables in the same system, or via inbound webservice from remote systems. Cash flows are the important information for Cash Managers to understand the short, mid and long term financial situation.

**Business Context**: The data product contains potential personal data intended to be used for managing sales and procurement contracts for energy solutions.

sap-odm-BillingDocument-v1.ShortText: A billing document is a set of data that can represent a customer invoice, credit memo, debit memo, pro forma invoice, or the corresponding cancellation document.
sap-odm-BillingDocument-v1.Description:
A billing document is a set of data that can represent a customer invoice, credit memo, debit memo, pro forma invoice, or the corresponding cancellation document. 

Every billing document consists of a header and a number of items. The header contains data that applies to the entire document, while items contain data that is only valid for the respective item. 

Most billing documents are posted to financial accounting to create the required journal entries for the relevant accounts (for example, accounts receivable).

The most common type of billing document is the customer invoice, which you use to request payment from customers for products you have supplied or services you have rendered.

Similarly, you can use credit memos to credit customers when you owe them money, as in the case of customer returns.

sap-odm-BillingDocumentRequest-v1.ShortText: A billing document request (BDR) is a set of data that acts as an intermediary business document between raw, itemized billable data and the subsequent billing documents.
sap-odm-BillingDocumentRequest-v1.Description:
A billing document request (BDR) is a set of data that acts as an intermediary business document between raw, itemized billable data and the subsequent billing documents. 

In a BDR, the system persists this billable data in a header-and-item-based document format. The header contains data that applies to the entire document (for example, the billing date and the bill-to party). The items contain data that is only valid for the respective item (for example, the sold product, its quantity, and its net value). 

 

BDRs serve to funnel itemized billable data from a range of system-internal and external sources into the billing process. For example, billable data originating from service transactions, from an imported spreadsheet file, or from an integrated external system can all be persisted in the system as BDRs.

BDRs can be billed, individually or together with other sales and distributions (SD) documents, to create customer invoices and other billing documents. They appear in the billing due list alongside other billable SD documents.

sap-odm-ConsolidationSubitem-v1.ShortText: A consolidation subitem is a value within a given subitem category in financial consolidation.
sap-odm-ConsolidationSubitem-v1.Description:
A consolidation subitem is a value within a given subitem category in financial consolidation. The subitem category together with the subitem may determine a further breakdown of a financial statement item. Whether such a further breakdown of a financial statement item by subitem category and subitem is mandatory, optionally allowed, or even not allowed is defined in the breakdown category which is assigned in the master data of the financial statement item.

Example values of subitem category 1 for transaction types are:

  • 900: Opening balance
  • 901: Incoming units

Example values of subitem category 2 for functional areas are:

  • YB10: Sales revenue
  • YB18: Cost of goods sold

sap-odm-ConsolidationVersion-v1.ShortText: A consolidation version is a distinct version of data in consolidation.
sap-odm-ConsolidationVersion-v1.Description:
A consolidation version is a distinct version of data in consolidation. In addition to a consolidation version for actual data, other versions of data that can be managed in parallel can be created, so that alternative results for the purposes of simulation, planning, and restatement can be produced. A consolidation version can be used for parallel processing with different data categories, accounting principles, and valuations, such as multiple group currencies.
To each consolidation version, special versions are assigned. The assignment of special versions enables the reuse of the maintained settings of a special version among different consolidation versions: The control parameters are entered only once in a special version and these settings are then reflected in all the consolidation versions to which the special version is assigned. Examples for special versions are data entry, consolidation unit attributes, financial statement item attributes, group structure, exchange rates, reclassification and elimination.

sap-odm-CostCenter-v1.ShortText: A cost center is an organizational unit that represents the location where costs are incurred.
sap-odm-CostCenter-v1.Description:
A cost center is an organizational unit that represents the location where costs are incurred.

Cost centers are used for the assignment of overhead costs to organizational activities based on the utilization of the relevant areas, as well as for differentiated management of costs arising in your organization.

Each cost center is assigned a category, depending on its type, such as Marketing (9), Production (F), Development (E), and other types.

sap-odm-CostCenterActivityType-v1.ShortText: A cost center activity type is a unit in a controlling area that classifies the activities performed in a cost center.
sap-odm-CostCenterActivityType-v1.Description:
A cost center activity type is a unit in a controlling area that classifies the activities performed in a cost center.

Activities are measured and recorded in units, such as machine hours, consulting hours, or units produced.

You can assign cost center activity types to one or multiple cost centers.

The allocation of the activities performed and price calculation are based on the respective cost rate ('AccountingCostRate') settings.

sap-odm-CreditMemoRequest-v1.ShortText: A credit memo request is a sales document used to propose a reduction in customer-specific receivables in the context of sales.
sap-odm-CreditMemoRequest-v1.Description:
A credit memo request is a sales document used to propose a reduction in customer-specific receivables in the context of sales. It is used to request a credit for a customer for reasons such as:

  • The customer returns goods previously purchased and needs to be credited for the returned items.
  • The customer asks for compensation for defective goods without returning them.
  • The customer has paid more than the invoiced amount and requests a credit to correct the excess amount.

Once approved, the system uses the credit memo request to create a credit memo.

sap-odm-DebitMemoRequest-v1.ShortText: A debit memo request is a sales document used to propose an increase in customer-specific receivables.
sap-odm-DebitMemoRequest-v1.Description:
A debit memo request is a sales document used to propose an increase in customer-specific receivables. It's used to request additional charges on a customer for reasons such as:

  • Incorrect pricing is carried out during the initial invoicing process, resulting in an undercharge.
  • Additional services or products are provided to the customer after the initial invoice is created.

Once approved, the system uses the debit memo request to create a debit memo for the customer, thereby starting the billing process for the additional charges.

sap-odm-EHSCalculationDefinition-v1.DisplayName: Environment and Health and Safety Calculation Definition
sap-odm-EHSCalculationDefinition-v1.ShortText: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) calculation definition is a calculation of operational data for a specific EHS location.
sap-odm-EHSCalculationDefinition-v1.Description: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) calculation definition is a calculation of operational data for a specific EHS location. Each calculation definition has an equation, a frequency, a unit of measurement, and a subject. It is used to determine the environmental impact of facilities, for example, the amount of air emissions of a given pollutant.

sap-odm-EHSDataAmount-v1.DisplayName: Environment and Health and Safety Data Amount
sap-odm-EHSDataAmount-v1.ShortText: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) data amount is a quantity of operational environmental data.
sap-odm-EHSDataAmount-v1.Description: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) data amount is a quantity of operational environmental data. It enables operational data analysis and accurate modeling and calculation of facility environmental impact. Air and wastewater emissions as well as sampling information can be assessed to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

sap-odm-EHSDataCollection-v1.DisplayName: Environment and Health and Safety Data Collection
sap-odm-EHSDataCollection-v1.ShortText: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) data collection is a collection of operational data for a specific EHS location.
sap-odm-EHSDataCollection-v1.Description: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) data collection is a collection of operational data for a specific EHS location. Each data collection has a defined frequency, unit of measurement, and subject. It is used to collect quantities of operational data to determine, calculate, or aggregate the environmental impact of facilities, such as the quantity of air emissions of a specific pollutant.

sap-odm-EHSLocation-v1.DisplayName: Environment and Health and Safety Location
sap-odm-EHSLocation-v1.ShortText: An environmental, health, and safety (EHS) location is a specific site or area within an organization that falls under the responsibility of the safety management team.
sap-odm-EHSLocation-v1.Description: An environmental, health, and safety (EHS) location is a specific site or area within an organization that falls under the responsibility of the safety management team. It can range from large areas like an entire plant to smaller spaces such as a staircase or the vicinity of a machine. Locations are structured logically to reflect their spatial or functional position within the company, aiding in incident management and data analysis.

sap-odm-EHSLocationAggregation-v1.ShortText: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) location aggregation is an entity that enables you to aggregate emissions data for a particular location, for the purpose of reporting to environmental authorities and ensuring compliance with legislation.
sap-odm-EHSLocationAggregation-v1.Description: An environment, health, and safety (EHS) location aggregation is an entity that enables you to aggregate emissions data for a particular location, for the purpose of reporting to environmental authorities and ensuring compliance with legislation. sap-odm-ExchangeRate-v1.ShortText: An exchange rate is a rate at which an amount is translated from one currency into another currency.
sap-odm-ExchangeRate-v1.Description: An exchange rate is a rate at which an amount is translated from one currency into another currency.

sap-odm-FunctionalLocation-v1.ShortText: A functional location is an organizational unit within Logistics that structures the maintenance objects of a company according to functional, process-related, or spatial criteria.
sap-odm-FunctionalLocation-v1.Description:
A functional location is an organizational unit within Logistics that structures the maintenance objects of a company according to functional, process-related, or spatial criteria. A functional location represents the place at which a maintenance task is to be performed.

Typical examples of functional location are:

  • Pumping station
  • Hall
  • Drive unit

sap-odm-Fund-v1.Description: A fund is an account assignment object that is used to represent financial resources provided by a public organization or a sponsor. The fund is the source of funding used for tracking, controlling and reporting for expenditures and revenues for a specific purpose.

sap-odm-GeneralLedgerAccount-v1.Description:
A general ledger account represents G/L Account Master Data in the Chart of Accounts area which contain information about the G/L account that are valid for all company codes. The chart of accounts area also contains data that control how a G/L account is created in the company code-specific area.

Examples:
(1) Information if the G/L Account is a Profit&Loss Account
(2) Description of the G/L Account

sap-odm-HouseBank-v1.ShortText: A house bank, in the context of SAP, is a bank that a company has a contract with.
sap-odm-HouseBank-v1.Description: A house bank, in the context of SAP, is a bank that a company has a contract with. House banks and house bank accounts are required for payment transactions and accounting in an SAP system. Each house bank is identified by the combination of the company code and house bank ID.

sap-odm-ListedSubstanceElement-v1.Description: A listed substance element is a listed substance, a listed substance variant, or a listed substance group. Listed substance elements are chemicals or substances (including certain compounds) that are described and regulated in the environmental authorities' official legislation.

sap-odm-PaymentTerms-v1.ShortText: Payment terms is a coded representation of terms of payment composed of cash discount percentages and payment periods.
sap-odm-PaymentTerms-v1.Description:
Payment terms is a coded representation of terms of payment composed of cash discount percentages and payment periods.
It is used in sales orders, purchase orders, and invoices. Terms of payment provide information for:
•Cash management
•Dunning procedures
•Payment transactions

Typical examples are:
2% cash discount 14 days, net due 30 days
Net due 14 days
Net due 30 days

sap-odm-PreliminaryBillingDocument-v1.ShortText: A preliminary billing document is a set of data that serves as an optional, intermediary business document between a billed reference document (for example, a billing document request) and the final billing document (usually an invoice).
sap-odm-PreliminaryBillingDocument-v1.Description:
A preliminary billing document is a set of data that serves as an optional, intermediary business document between a billed reference document (for example, a billing document request) and the final billing document (usually an invoice).
 
Preliminary billing documents are almost identical to standard billing documents in form and content, but are created purely for negotiation purposes. Like billing documents, preliminary billing documents consist of a header and a number of items. The header contains data that applies to the entire document (for example, the billing date and the bill-to party), while the items contain data that is only valid for the respective item (for example, the sold product, its quantity, and its net value). 
 
Preliminary billing documents are relevant for output (for example, print), but not for posting to financial accounting.

sap-odm-Product-v1.ShortText: A product is a good that contributes to a company's value chain by being traded.
sap-odm-Product-v1.Description: A product is a good that contributes to a company's value chain by being traded.  It can either be tangible or intangible. Tangible products are physical goods, like materials or finished items. Intangible products are services or digital goods.

sap-odm-ProductGroup-v1.ShortText: A product group is a key that defines a group of products that have the same attributes.
sap-odm-ProductGroup-v1.Description: A product group is a key that defines a group of products that have the same attributes. Product groups are commonly created in order to restrict the scope of analyses. E.g., an industrial tools manufacturer could create product groups such as hand tools, power tools, hydraulic tools, measuring tools, etc.

sap-odm-ProductionOrderConfirmation-v1.ShortText: A production order confirmation is a document that records the processing status of a production order, its operations, and sub-operations.
sap-odm-ProductionOrderConfirmation-v1.Description: A production order confirmation is a document that records the processing status of a production order, its operations, and sub-operations. Specifically, it documents the quantities of produced goods (yield and/or scrap), the quantity of produced goods to be reworked, the work center at which the operation was carried out, who performed the operations, the time spent, as well as the values for the work activities.

sap-odm-ProductionVersion-v1.ShortText: A production version is a specific method or technique used to manufacture a particular material.
sap-odm-ProductionVersion-v1.Description: A production version is a specific method or technique used to manufacture a particular material. It essentially combines a bill of material (BOM) and a production routing/master recipe to outline the production process. It determines which alternative BOM is used with which production routing/master recipe to produce or plan a material.

sap-odm-ProfitCenter-v1.ShortText: A profit center is an organizational unit in accounting that reflects a management-oriented structure of the organization for the purpose of internal control.
sap-odm-ProfitCenter-v1.Description:
A profit center is an organizational unit in accounting that reflects a management-oriented structure of the organization for the purpose of internal control.

This organizational unit represents an area of a company for which a separate period-based profit is determined and used for profit-oriented analysis and management of the area´s activities.

sap-odm-Project-v1.ShortText: A project is a structured endeavor with defined objectives, timelines, and budgets to achieve a unique outcome.
sap-odm-Project-v1.Description:
A project is a structured endeavor with defined objectives, timelines, and budgets to achieve a unique outcome.  A project is characterized by a unique set of conditions on which it is based (for example, the targets to be met, the organizational structure, and the financial, personal, staffing and time constraints on the project).

 
In the Project System application projects can be structured and controlled via a work breakdown structure (WBS), consisting of a project definition and WBS elements, which can be arranged in a hierarchical way. In addition you can use networks and network activities assigned to WBS elements in Project System e.g. to schedule dates, manage capacities, or plan and trigger the procurement of services and materials.

sap-odm-ProjectServiceOrganization-v1.ShortText: A project service organization represents an organizational unit that delivers services in a project and is responsible for executing and delivering a project.
sap-odm-ProjectServiceOrganization-v1.Description:
A project service organization represents an organizational unit that delivers services in a project and is responsible for executing and delivering a project.
In SAP S/4HANA Cloud, professional services the project service organization is used while setting up an internal or a customer project. Project service organizations are defined in the "Maintain Service Organization" App alongside the following attributes:
Sales Organization: to indicate that the organization is responsible only for the delivery of projects.
Delivery Organization: to indicate that the organization can provide the resources needed to deliver project services
Cost center: the assigned cost centers are used to determine cost rates in projects, and to staff resources

sap-odm-SalesArea-v1.ShortText: A sales area is a specific combination of a sales organization, a distribution channel, and a division.
sap-odm-SalesArea-v1.Description: A sales area is a specific combination of a sales organization, a distribution channel, and a division. It is used in sales and distribution documents, such as sales orders, invoices, and outbound deliveries.

sap-odm-SalesBillOfMaterial-v1.ShortText: A sales bill of material is a list of components and their quantities that make up a top-level material for a sales order.
sap-odm-SalesBillOfMaterial-v1.Description:
A sales bill of material is a list of components and their quantities that make up a top-level material for a sales order.

The object is used in sales order processing.

sap-odm-SalesContract-v1.Description: A sales contract is a legally binding agreement that contains special conditions negotiated between the supplier and a customer for products to be sold to the customer over a specified period. A sales contract represents a long-term relationship between the supplier and the customer.

sap-odm-SalesGroup-v1.Description: A sales group is an organizational unit that subdivides a sales office according to specific needs, for example, according to areas of responsibility.

sap-odm-SalesInquiry-v1.Description: A sales inquiry is a request from a customer to a sales organization for a quotation or sales information that is not binding. It is accepted by the sales area that is then responsible for any further processing.

sap-odm-SalesOffice-v1.ShortText: A sales office is an organizational unit responsible for sales within a geographical area of a sales organization.
sap-odm-SalesOffice-v1.Description: A sales office is an organizational unit responsible for sales within a geographical area of a sales organization. It can be viewed as an actual office or perhaps a territory or region. A sales office establishes contact between the company and the regional market.

sap-odm-SalesOrder-v1.ShortText: A sales order is an agreement between a sales organization and a customer on the sale of products (goods or services).
sap-odm-SalesOrder-v1.Description:
A sales order is an agreement between a sales organization and a customer on the sale of products (goods or services). It lays down the conditions that both parties accept: the delivery of a specific quantity for a defined price at a certain time.
A sales order is a specific sales document category that initiates the fulfilment process and helps maintain an accurate inventory.

sap-odm-SalesOrderWithoutCharge-v1.ShortText: A sales order without charge is an agreement between a sales organization and a customer on the provisioning of products (goods or services).
sap-odm-SalesOrderWithoutCharge-v1.Description:
A sales order without charge is an agreement between a sales organization and a customer on the provisioning of products (goods or services). It lays down the conditions that both parties accept: the delivery of a specific quantity at a certain time free of charge.
A sales order without charge is a specific sales document category that is used, for example, to ship product samples, promotional items, or replacements.

sap-odm-SalesOrganization-v1.Description: A sales organization is an organizational unit that subdivides a company according to its sales requirements, for example, geographically into countries or regions. It is used in sales and distribution documents, such as sales orders, invoices, and outbound deliveries.

sap-odm-SalesQuotation-v1.ShortText: A sales quotation is an offer from a sales organization containing price and date commitments for specific products to be sold to potential customers.
sap-odm-SalesQuotation-v1.Description: A sales quotation is an offer from a sales organization containing price and date commitments for specific products to be sold to potential customers. The offer binds the supplier for a certain period of time and provides information for customers to make purchasing decisions.

sap-odm-SalesSchedulingAgreement-v1.Description: A sales scheduling agreement is an agreement that outlines the expected quantity of products to be delivered to the customer over a specific period of time. sap-odm-SecuritiesAccount-v1.Description: A securities account is a unit used for position management and valuation. A securities account is required for all financial transactions that require position management. Typically, a securities account in the SAP system relates to an actual securities account at a bank.

sap-odm-SecurityClass-v1.ShortText: A security class is a dataset that defines a securities product.
sap-odm-SecurityClass-v1.Description: A security class is a dataset that defines a securities product. It contains all relevant conditions, like issue date, condition structure, stock exchanges, etc. for an individual product category, such as stocks, bonds, etc.

sap-odm-StatisticalKeyFigure-v1.Description:
A statistical key figure is a number that provides information about non-monetary data relating to organizational units.

This object can be used to track measurable characteristics of organizational units, such as cost centers and profit centers, in addition to monetary data from accounting.

sap-odm-StorageLocation-v1.ShortText: A storage location is a specific location, where stock is stored in a plant.
sap-odm-StorageLocation-v1.Description: A storage location is a specific location, where stock is stored in a plant. This location is also used to differentiate different type of stocks within a plant.

sap-odm-WorkCenter-v1.Description: A work center is an area or section of a production facility where production operations are performed. Machines, Machine Group, Production line and People represent the work center that are used to perform the required production order operations.

sap-odm-WorkCenterGroup-v1.ShortText: A work center group is a grouping of work centers according to capacity requirements planning criteria.
sap-odm-WorkCenterGroup-v1.Description: A work center group is a grouping of work centers according to capacity requirements planning criteria. A work center group is used in capacity planning to cumulate available capacity and capacity requirements. By assigning multiple work centers under one work center group, one can immediately view the work center's capacity demands and remaining capacities aggregated into a work center group. A work center group may contain further group(s) within it.

sap-odm-WorkforceCapability-v1.Description:
A workforce capability is a skill, competency, certification, and other types of capability that are typically of interest to employer based on the industry of operation, and it includes attribute name, description, and other data such as attribute type. Workforce capability is assigned to one or more workforce capability catalog.
Workforce person acquires or becomes proficient in one or more capability over a period of time.

sap-odm-WorkforceCapabilityCatalog-v1.Description: A workforce capability catalog is a list of skills, competencies, certifications, and other types of capabilities that are typically of interest to employer based on the industry of operation, and it includes attribute name, description, and other data such as attribute type.

sap-odm-WorkforceCapabilityProficiencySc.ShortText: A workforce capability proficiency scale is a rating scale on which a workforce person's proficiency is rated.
sap-odm-WorkforceCapabilityProficiencySc.Description: A workforce capability proficiency scale is a rating scale on which a workforce person's proficiency is rated. Each workforce capability can have a proficiency rating scale. Workforce person has capabilities and the rating a user has, if present, and this rating needs to be presented/understood in the context of the scale on which it is placed.
